title: Simplified quantum key distribution implementation secure in the presence of state preparation flaws
authors: Ainhoa Agulleiro, Fadri Grünenfelder, Raphaël Houlmann, Ana Blázquez, Hugo Zbinden, Davide Rusca
abstract: We present an implementation of a three-state BB84 protocol with time-bin encoding, one decoy state and a simplified measurement scheme that uses passive basis choice. Our system simplifies the state characterization with respect to previous iterations. We also adapt the loss-tolerant method to our protocol, thus dealing with the measured state preparation flaws. We compare the obtained phase error rate and secret key rate when including the state imperfections and when assuming perfect states. Our results highlight the importance of characterization and implementation security.
summary: This paper presents an experimental implementation of a three-state BB84 Quantum Key Distribution protocol designed to be secure despite common State Preparation Flaws. By adapting the Loss-Tolerant method and characterizing these flaws using decoy states, the authors demonstrate key rate security over long distances while accounting for non-ideal hardware performance.
main_problem: The primary goal is to implement a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol that maintains security guarantees even when accounting for realistic State Preparation Flaws (SPFs).
main_result: The work successfully adapts the Loss-Tolerant method to ensure secret key distribution remains secure against collective attacks over 150km of fiber without assuming perfect state preparation.
method: The authors use a three-state BB84 protocol with time-bin encoding and adapt the Loss-Tolerant method to incorporate measurements derived from decoy states, allowing for security analysis under imperfect conditions.
model_or_system: The system is an experimental QKD setup using superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) and a three-state BB84 protocol. Alice's side uses time-bin encoding, while Bob employs passive basis choice for measurement.
key_observables: Phase error rate ($\phi_Z$) and secret key rate (SKR).
important_parameters: Fiber length (up to 151km), detector efficiency ($\eta=90\%$), mean photon numbers ($\mu_0, \mu_1$).
main_assumptions: The security analysis is limited to collective attacks; the characterization method incorporates visibility due to delay mismatch naturally.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the schematic of states at different stages. Figure 2 details the experimental setup on Alice's and Bob's sides, while subsequent figures plot measured state angles ($	heta, \phi$) and simulate error rates/SKR dependence on these angles.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from describing the physical implementation (Alice/Bob setups) to detailing the measurement diagnostics (SPFs characterization), culminating in the theoretical adaptation of security bounds (Loss-Tolerant method) for finite-key analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical, experimentally validated framework for assessing QKD security under real-world imperfections like state preparation flaws, which is crucial for advancing quantum communication technology.
